decision: Hire Marcus Feld as VP Engineering on his stated terms

framing.context: Marcus Feld ran a 40-person robotics org and would be the strongest engineering leader we could get at our stage. His terms: 4.0% equity on a standard 4-year vest with a full-acceleration single trigger, a board observer seat, and sole authority over the engineering roadmap. Our entire remaining option pool is 6.2%. Two of our three senior engineers have said privately they would report to him happily; the third, Riley, says he would leave. Our largest customer's program depends on Riley's calibration pipeline.
options: Counter: 2.5% with milestone vesting, no board seat, roadmap shared with CEO

members.name: Alex
members.decisive_reason: I will not trade governance for a hire, however good.

answers.P1_timing: He has a competing offer he says closes 2026-08-15. I have not verified it.
answers.P2_reversibility: 1-way on the equity and the board observer seat. The title is reversible; the cap table and the board are not.
answers.P3_expected_value: With him we probably ship the v2 release two quarters earlier. Without him I keep running engineering myself and we slip.
answers.P4_downside_cap: Worst case is 4% gone, a board observer who is not aligned, and Riley out the door in the same quarter.
answers.P5_opportunity_cost: 4.0% is two-thirds of the remaining pool. That is the next eight senior hires.
answers.P6_information: Whether his competing offer is real, and whether Riley's threat to leave is a position or an interest.
answers.P7_second_order: A board observer seat granted to an employee sets the precedent for every future senior hire and complicates the Series A.
answers.P8_strategy_fit: Great operator fit, bad governance fit.
answers.P9_owner: Me, but the board must approve equity over 3%.
answers.P10_kill_criteria: If he has not shipped a working v2 integration in two quarters we have mispriced him.

members.name: Jordan
members.decisive_reason: We are eighteen months behind because nobody is running engineering full time.

answers.P1_timing: Now. Every week Alex runs engineering is a week ops runs itself.
answers.P2_reversibility: Mostly 2-way. Equity vests over four years; a bad hire is fired in six months and keeps very little.
answers.P3_expected_value: Two quarters of schedule is worth more than 1.5% of dilution.
answers.P4_downside_cap: Firing him at six months costs us 0.5% vested and a quarter of churn.
answers.P5_opportunity_cost: The alternative is Alex staying as de facto VP Eng, which is the actual bottleneck.
answers.P6_information: Backchannel references on how he handles disagreement with a founder.
answers.P7_second_order: A real VP Eng lets us hire eight engineers who would not join without a leader.
answers.P8_strategy_fit: Yes. Execution speed is the strategy.
answers.P10_kill_criteria: No engineering hire made by him within 90 days.

members.name: Riley
members.decisive_reason: Sole roadmap authority means the calibration pipeline gets rewritten by someone who has never seen our sensor data.

answers.P1_timing: There is no real deadline. The competing offer is almost certainly leverage.
answers.P2_reversibility: 1-way in the way that matters: if the calibration pipeline is rewritten, the customer program is unrecoverable this year.
answers.P3_expected_value: Best case he is great and we still lose a quarter to reorganisation. Worst case he replaces the one system that works.
answers.P4_downside_cap: The downside is the customer program, not the equity.
answers.P5_opportunity_cost: The same 4% would fund three calibration engineers who could actually parallelise my work.
answers.P6_information: Ask him what he would do with the calibration pipeline in his first 90 days. His answer decides it.
answers.P7_second_order: Sole roadmap authority removes the CEO from technical arbitration permanently.
answers.P8_strategy_fit: No. Our moat is calibration data, not org chart depth.
answers.P9_owner: Alex decides, but I want it on record that I would not stay under sole roadmap authority.
answers.P10_kill_criteria: If he touches the calibration pipeline before the customer milestone, that is the failure signal.
